thread:
ada: Heads-up: planning an 'eviction blast' game day next Wed 09:30 PT. Goal is to validate mixed-capacity fallback paths and rollback behavior when spot GPUs are evicted.

miguel: +1. can we scope it to only staging and a small percentage of traffic? don't want surprises. :grimacing:

sasha: i'd prefer 5% canary -> 0% if anything spikes. we'll run 3 rounds of forced evictions spaced 10m apart.

kai: sounds good. propose targeting these success criteria: 1) <2% error-rate delta vs baseline, 2) median p99 token-latency increase <40%, 3) autoscaler moves 60% of evicted work into dedicated pool within 120s.
lina: can we add cache-warmup check? if we fallback to on-demand variant we should measure KV cache thrash.
adea: (typo) ada: yep, add cache miss-rate and token cost delta to metrics.

miguel: quick runbook sketch:
- create ephemeral ASG/instance-group: name=preempt-blast-staging
- mark subset of nodes as spot-only via label `node.k8s.aws/spot=true`
- deploy experiment stack with canary route `canary/eviction-blast` at 5%
- cron job to terminate random spot instances (aws ec2 terminate-instances or gcloud instances delete)
- observe fallback router -> decision tree: try same model quantized variant on dedicated, else route to lower-cost model fallback

kai: include command snippets in runbook (for ops runner):
```
kubectl label node ip-10-0-3-4 node.k8s.aws/spot=true
aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0abc1234
# or simulate via devops-runner which interacts with cloud provider safely
```

sasha: devops-runner: can your job enforce a max of 2 concurrent terminations? we want gradual degradation.
devops-runner: yes, we have a controller that can randomize with concurrency param. i'll share the executor link in the runbook.

lina: monitoring checklist:
- grafana panel: evictions/min, node count, pods pending, pods restarting
- traces: span drop / preempted request handoff
- cost dashboard: token-unit cost vs baseline (hourly)
- alert: sustained 500s > 1% for 10m -> abort game day

miguel: abort criteria: any SLO breach on production-like endpoints or pager triggers from oncall. This is staging-only but if any cross-region replication tasks fail we stop.

ada: ada: who will drive canary rollback if we see regressions?
kai: i'll own rollback. sasha will coordinate with oncall.

sasha: small UX note: the router logs currently say `fallback=unknown` for a subset of requests. let's add richer reason codes before the blast. can the router team PR a patch by EOD Fri?
miguel: i'll ping router team. they owe us a quick change: `fallback_reason=dedicated_capacity` etc.

lina: experiment matrix we will record per-run:
- run id, forced-evictions (n), canary-traffic(%), baseline p95/p99, fallback latency, cache-miss-rate, tokens-consumed, cost-delta

ada: devops-runner: please instrument run ids into logs like `evblast.run=1765432109.r1` so we can aggregate.
devops-runner: will do.

oncall-bot: reminder: oncall rotation this week: @lina (primary), @sasha (secondary). Escalation policy unchanged.

miguel: volunteers for observers? we want an SRE, runtime eng, infra eng, and product rep.
kai: i'm runtime eng, in.
sasha: infra + me. ada: i can represent product. lina: SRE here.

lina: quick pre-checks (to run 30m before):
- ensure canary route is at 0% then bump to 5% with terraform apply
- snapshot autoscaler config: `min=2, scale_up_cooldown=30s`
- ensure pyroscope/profiler sampling for fallback models is ON

miguel: after-run retro agenda: what failed, why router picked fallback variant, how long eviction events lasted, cost impact, follow-ups (patches + runbook updates).

ada: expected duration ~90m including validation and cool-down. keep the service desk runbook open.

sasha: run plan approval: if no objections by EOD Tue i'm greenlighting.

kai: one ask: add a step to validate KV cache TTL settings on fallback model start. high churn kills perf.
lina: noted. i'll add TTL measurement to checklist.

miguel: small note on cost modelling: the simulation will capture immediate cost delta but we should estimate normalized monthly cost impact if we used 30% spot vs 60% spot. i'll attach a quick calc after the exercise.

ada: final: leaving the doc here + runbook link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/eviction-blast-runbook (will update with command snippets and executor link). pls react :thumbsup: if you can make next Wed 09:30 PT.

sasha: :thumbsup:
kai: :thumbsup:
lina: :thumbsup:
miguel: :thumbsup:

ada: post-mortem note (after run): round 1 we saw 85% of evicted requests re-routed to dedicated pool within 55s. cache miss spike +45%, p99 increased by 28%. autoscaler failed to spin up one node due to subnet IP exhaustion — we capped by default `max_nodes` in tf. follow-ups: bump subnet / adjust pool headroom, add pre-check to simulate IP allocation, and add router reason codes.

sasha: retro action: add a preflight check to fail the run early if `available_ips < 10` in the target subnet. i'll own that patch.
kai: cost note: during the 90m window token-cost increased by ~12% due to more expensive dedicated variants; projected monthly impact if spikes frequent would be non-trivial. recommend trying a lower-cost fallback model next run.

lina: marking experiment PASS for the routing logic, FAIL for autoscaler safety nets. moving to actions.

miguel: great data. will write the retro doc and capture metrics. thanks everyone.

oncall-bot: automated summary posted to #incidents as incident-capture/1765432109 for archival.
